sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellants contends that the impugned common award dated 14.02.2023 passed by the learned Tribunal is unjust, illegal 1 of 5 FAO-2166-2023 23 (O&M) -2- and arbitrary,
as it has awarded a meager compensation despite the fact that both claim petitions arise out of the the same accident dated 21.05.2020, caused solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Bolero P Pick-Up Up bearing registration No.HR-62A-6498 6498 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) driven by respondent No.1, who came on the wrong side side of the road and hit the motorcycle of the deceased, resulting in the death of Sharawan Kumar as well as his minor son Mukesh Kumar.

Furthermore, F , the learned Tribunal erred in not granting filial consortium to the parents of the deceased in terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram and others, 2018 (4) RCR (civil) 333 and reiterated in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
644.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram and others, 2018 (4) RCR (civil) 333
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
644
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Additionally Somwati and others, 2020 (9) SCC 644.

Additionally,, in the case of death of Sharawan arawan Kumar aged 37 3 years, the learned Tribunal has erroneously assessed his monthly income @Rs.13,050/- per month whereas he was a Mason by profession and therefore, at least leas his income ought to have been taken Rs.15,000/ Rs.15,000/- per month, month applied an incorrect multiplier and granted inadequate compensation under the conventional heads.

Subsequently, S , in the case of death of minor Mukesh Kumar aged 11 years, the learned Tribunal has committed a patent illegality by awarding a lump sum compensation, ignoring the settled settled principle that a minor victim cannot be equated with a non-earning non earning person and that minimum wages applicable to a skilled worker are required to be adopted along with multiplier and future prospects as of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Karuna Parmar v. Prakash Sinha, 2025 INSC 1244 and judgment rendered by this Court in Rakesh Kumar Vs. 155673.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently,, the learned Deepak Kumar and others 2025 PHHC 155673 Tribunal also committed an error in not awarding adequate rate of interest, though the he appellants were legally entitled to higher interest from the date of filing of the 2 of 5 FAO-2166-2023 23 (O&M) -3- claim petitions till realization.

entities.text: Deepak Kumar and others 2025 PHHC 155673 Tribunal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lastly, L , it is submitted that the entire approach of the learned Tribunal is contrary to law and evidence on record, thereby necessitating necessitatin interference by this Hon'ble Court for enhancement of compensation in both the connected appeals by passing a common order.

3. Per contra, contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 submits that the award passed by the learned Tribunal does not suffer from any irregularity or infirmity, and that the findings recorded therein are well- Nirmla Devi vs Malkit Alias Malkiyat And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173304048/
2 well-reasoned reasoned on the basis of the material available before the learned learned Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is accordingly contended that no ground is made out for interference in appeal.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the record, with their able assistance.
5. The Motor Vehicles Act, Act 1988 is a beneficial and we welfare lfare legislation intended to provide just, fair and reasonable compensation to victims of motor accidents and their families.

The objective of the statute is not to award token amounts but to ensure restitution, to the extent possible, for the loss suffer suffered.
ed.

In the present case, for the death of minor Mukesh Kumar, aged about 11 years, the learned Tribunal awarded a lump-sum lump sum compensation of 3,00,000/- whereas in the case of death of a school going child, notional income ought to have been taken.

Learned counsel ounsel for the appellants has rightly placed reliance upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Karuna Parmar v. Prakash Sinha Sinha,, 2025 INSC 1244,, wherein it has been held that a minor victim cannot be equated with a non- non earning person and that the income income of such a victim must be assessed on the basis of minimum wages applicable to a skilled worker, with addition of future prospects and application of the appropriate multiplier.

entities.text: Karuna Parmar v. Prakash Sinha Sinha,, 2025 INSC 1244
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similar principles have been reiterated 3 of 5 FAO-2166-2023 23 (O&M)
-4- by this Court in Rakesh Kumar v. Deepak eepak Kumar and others others,, 2025 PHHC 155673.
6.

entities.text: Rakesh Kumar v. Deepak eepak Kumar and others others,, 2025 PHHC 155673
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to reassess the income of Therefore, the deceased minor on the basis of minimum wages.

Since the accident occurred in District Hisar on 21.05.2020,
the minimum wages applicable in the State of Haryana as on the said date are required to be adopted.
The minimum wage wages for a skilled worker at the relevant time were 8798//- per month.
Accordingly, the annual income of the deceased dece is assessed at 1,05,576 1,05,576/-..
After deducting 50% towards towar personal and living expenses, the annual contribution tto o the family comes to 52,788/-..

Further, adding 40% towards future prospects, the annual loss of dependency as mandated by law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Limited v. Pranay Sethi 2017 (16) SCC 680 and National Insurance Company Limited Smt. Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 2009 (6) SCC 121, it works out to 73,903/-..

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Smt. Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 2009 (6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the multiplier of 18, keeping in view the aforesaid judgments, the total loss of dependency is assessed at 13,30,254/-..
Consequently, the total compensation payable in the case of death of minor Mukesh Kumar is reassessed at 14,14,954/-,, as against 3,00,000/- awarded by the learned Tribunal.

7. In so far as the claim of compensation qua Sharawan Kumar, aged about 37 years, is concerned,
he was working as a Mason and therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to take the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/ Rs.15,000/- per month, which results in an annual income of 1,80,000/

3 80,000/-,, out of which, after deducting one- one 4 of 5 FAO-2166-2023 23 (O&M) -5- fourth towards personal expenses, the annual dependency comes to 1,35,000/.

entities.text: Nirmla Devi vs Malkit Alias Malkiyat And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On adding 40% towards future prospects, the annual loss of dependency works out to 1,89,000/-..
However, the learned Tribunal failed to apply the appropriate multiplier and granted inadequate compensation under the conventional heads, particularly filial consortium as per the law.

Applying the correct multiplier of 16, the loss of dependency is assessed at 30,24,000/
30,24,000/-.

In addition thereto, o, the claimants are entitled to 18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and 1,93,600/- (48,400x4) towards filial consortium payable to the parents (escalation @10% every three years as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra)).
)).

Consequently, the total compensation payable is reassessed at 32,53,900/-
32,5 as against 23,42,400/ 23,42,400/- awarded by the learned Tribunal.

The impugned award,
therefore, warrants interference to the aforesaid extent.

8. The enhanced compensation, i.e. over and above the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal, shall also carry interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization, payable by the respondent No.3 to the appellants-claimants appellants claimants in equal ratios.
9. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the award passed by the learned Tribunal is modified and the present appeal is allowed to the above extent.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
